headline: Semiconductors Buck a Broad Retreat as Iran Tensions and Soft Retail Data Weigh on Monday's Session
body_html:
Wall Street closed Monday's session in the red, with declining issues outnumbering advancers by a wide margin — 346 names lower against just 201 higher across our 550-name universe. The dominant pressure came from two fronts: geopolitical anxiety surrounding Iran's escalating rhetoric in the Strait of Hormuz, and fresh evidence of strain in the consumer economy, as retail results disappointed and consumer-facing equities fell 1.38% as a group. Software stocks, meanwhile, surrendered much of last week's momentum, sliding 1.90% to rank as Monday's worst-performing sector.

Against that dour backdrop, semiconductors stood apart, gaining 1.71% and claiming the session's only meaningful sector advance. The move was broad-based and conviction-driven: Semtech surged 9.88%, Sandisk added 8.88%, Credo Technology climbed 8.82%, and optical-networking specialist Coherent rose 7.79%. Power-module maker Vicor Corporation joined the rally with a 7.99% gain. Chipmakers appeared to draw fresh attention from analyst commentary, even as the wider market struggled.

The session's single most dramatic move belonged to argenx, the immunology-focused biotech, which vaulted 16.04% on new clinical data — a sharp contrast to the losses endured by device makers STAAR Surgical and Align Technology, which fell 7.98% and 5.60%, respectively. With gold showing tentative signs of reclaiming safe-haven status after weeks of war-related selling, Monday's tape carried an unmistakable tone of selective risk reduction heading into a week heavy with geopolitical crosscurrents.

briefs.headline: Iran's Hormuz Warning Casts Shadow Over Energy Markets
briefs.body: Tehran signaled it could shift to offensive operations in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomatic talks with Washington break down. The threat injected fresh uncertainty into global energy-supply calculations, though Energy sector equities in our universe managed a modest 0.27% gain on Monday, the second-best sectoral performance of the session.

briefs.headline: argenx Surges 16% on Fresh Clinical Data, Leading the Entire Universe
briefs.body: Immunology biotech argenx posted the largest single-session gain across our 550-name universe, climbing 16.04% after new medical data emerged. The move set the stock apart from a broadly weak Healthcare sector, which dipped 0.17% on the day, weighed down by steep declines in device makers.

briefs.headline: Consumer Stocks Among Hardest Hit as Retail Results Disappoint
briefs.body: Consumer-oriented equities dropped 1.38% Monday, with retail results coming in below expectations and dragging sentiment across the group. Victoria's Secret fell 5.53% and H&R Block shed 7.03%, while Corsair Gaming slid 5.77%, reflecting broad pressure on spending-sensitive names.

briefs.headline: Software Gives Back Last Week's Gains in Broad Retreat
briefs.body: The software sector dropped 1.90%, reversing a meaningful portion of the prior week's advance. ZoomInfo was among the hardest hit, tumbling 7.16%. The reversal suggests last week's move lacked the fundamental follow-through needed to sustain momentum into a macro-uncertain week.

briefs.headline: Union Pacific Fuel-Surcharge Controversy Draws Scrutiny
briefs.body: Railroad operator Union Pacific faces questions after a report found that fuel surcharges — originally structured to offset costs tied to the Iran conflict — were instead converted into profit. The disclosure raises regulatory and reputational concerns for the freight industry at a politically sensitive moment.

briefs.headline: Gold Tentatively Reclaims Safe-Haven Footing After War-Driven Selloff
briefs.body: Precious metals showed early signs of renewed demand Monday as investors sought protection amid escalating Iran-related uncertainty. Gold had sold off sharply during the initial Iran war period, and analysts note the current move, while nascent, may signal a broader rotation back toward defensive assets if diplomacy continues to falter.
